title: Bachelor/Masters thesis protocol
author: Eliza Harris
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7brhim6
materials: Protocol: Bachelor and Master thesis students
Each table you produce needs a separate entry
Thank you for your data preservation efforts!

steps.title: Bachelor and master thesis students are...
steps.instruction: Bachelor and master thesis students are requested to follow this protocol upon completion of their project, to preserve data and results for use in future studies.

steps.title: Enter the details of your thesis in the excel sheet:
steps.instruction: Enter the details of your thesis in the excel sheet:

steps.title: Take care to follow the formatting...
steps.instruction: Take care to follow the formatting used for all other entries!

steps.title: If possible, add a contact email...
steps.instruction: If possible, add a contact email where you can be reached after you leave UIBK

steps.title: Name your thesis file (pdf only
steps.instruction: Name your thesis file (pdf only!) using the “ID” and save in the correct folder, eg. Bachelor_Theses, Master_Theses

steps.title: Organise your final data into one or more tables, eg
steps.instruction: Organise your final data into one or more tables, eg. a time column and associated variable columns.

steps.title: This should be the final data...
steps.instruction: This should be the final data you used for analysis, with calibrations/corrections/flagging performed. It should not include your analyses eg. temporal averaging, statistics, figures, tables.

steps.title: Make sure all variable names use...
steps.instruction: Make sure all variable names use only alphanumeric characters as well as “_” and “-“ with no spaces.

steps.title: Do not use special German characters...
steps.instruction: Do not use special German characters like ü or ß, and ensure all text is in English.

steps.title: This should only include “your” data...
steps.instruction: This should only include “your” data – group data like Kaserstatt micrometeorology does not need to be included unless you have added particular variables.

steps.title: Variable metadata
steps.instruction: Variable metadata: a table listing each variable in each of your data tables, and describing the variable in full, for example for CO2_5 metadata could include (but is not limited to!):

steps.title: Experimental metadata
steps.instruction: Experimental metadata: A clear description of all important features of your experiment. Most commonly a table with dates/times and events, eg. mowing, drought start, soil samples collected. This should also include overarching data eg. data owner, contact.

steps.title: Site metadata
steps.instruction: Site metadata: If your site is not already listed, you will need to add it to ecophysiology_newstructure/Server_DataList.xlsx, tab “Sites”

steps.title: Make your metadata detailed
steps.instruction: Make your metadata detailed! Assume the person using it to interpret your data has no prior knowledge of what you have done.

steps.title: Speak to Eliza or Johnny if...
steps.instruction: Speak to Eliza or Johnny if you are not sure how to prepare your metadata.

steps.title: Put the following header (or similar)...
steps.instruction: Put the following header (or similar) as the very first line in all your datasheets – this will ensure if someone obtains just this table they know where it originates from: “This dataset includes SHORT DESCRIPTION OF YOUR DATA. This data may only be used with the permission of the dataset owners; co-authorship must be offered for publications utilising this data. Dataset owners: YOUR NAME, Michael Bahn. Contact: YOUR EMAIL, michael.bahn@uibk.ac.at.”

steps.title: Enter the details of your data in the excel sheet:
steps.instruction: Enter the details of your data in the excel sheet:

steps.title: Take care to follow the formatting...
steps.instruction: Take care to follow the formatting used for all other entries!

steps.title: If possible, add a contact email...
steps.instruction: If possible, add a contact email where you can be reached after you leave UIBK

steps.title: Give your data tables an ID
steps.instruction: Give your data tables an ID: This needs to be 10 characters, no spaces, and unique. It should not include your name or the year of submission, as you will enter this in the “Publications” column, which shows the publications associated with this data. It should be as informative as possible regarding the contents of the data.

steps.title: Save all data and metadata as either
steps.instruction: Save all data and metadata as either .xlsx, .txt or .csv – not .pdf or .docx, and include in a folder on ecophysiology_newstructure/Data/ that is named according to your DatasetID

steps.title: Tables should be named DatasetID
steps.instruction: Tables should be named DatasetID.txt and associated metadata DatasetID_metadata.txt

steps.title: Code associated with your data that...
steps.instruction: Code associated with your data that others may find useful can be included in your Dataset folder and should be well commented and explained.

steps.title: The dataset N2O_CH4_KS and associated publication...
steps.instruction: The dataset N2O_CH4_KS and associated publication “Harris2018” can be used as an example.

steps.title: Once you are done, let me know (eliza
steps.instruction: Once you are done, let me know (eliza.harris@uibk.ac.at) so I can add it to the database.
